issues.description: The solution repository defines animal classes with 'Space' prefixes (SpaceGoat, SpacePig, SpaceSeal) while the problem specification and template expect classes named Goat, Pig, and Seal. This mismatch in class names/types creates a structural conflict: students will implement Goat/Pig/Seal as instructed and the template Main refers to those names, but the provided solution uses different types. This can confuse students about the correct class names and break any guidance or reference code comparing to the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution repository use the same class names as the specification and template (Goat, Pig, Seal). Either rename the Space* classes to Goat/Pig/Seal and adjust their implementations, or add wrapper classes Goat/Pig/Seal that delegate to the Space* implementations so the class names and types used across problem, template, and solution are consistent.

issues.description: The template's Farm.java declares a private helper method singFarmSongVerse without an Animal parameter (singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), but the UML/problem statement and the solution expect singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). The missing parameter in the template is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about the intended method signature and how to implement singFarmSong and verse printing.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Farm.java to declare singFarmSongVerse with the Animal parameter: private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). Adjust the method body to use that parameter (e.g., animal.getClass().getSimpleName() and animal.messageOnFeed()). This aligns the template with the UML and the solution and prevents confusion about the expected signature.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat, but the solution repository implements these concepts with differently named classes (SpaceSeal, SpacePig, SpaceGoat) while the expected class files Seal.java, Pig.java, Goat.java in the solution are empty. This mismatch breaks the one-to-one mapping between the conceptual entities described in the exercise and the concrete class names in the solution, likely confusing students about which classes to implement or inspect.
issues.suggestedFix: Use consistent class names across all artifacts. Rename the solution classes SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat to Seal, Pig, and Goat (or alternatively update the problem and template to reference SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat). Ensure Seal.java, Pig.java, and Goat.java are implemented (or delegate to the Space* classes) so the class names match the problem description and template code.
